items.name: mockio-theme
items.title: Mockio tokens
items.description: Both themes as CSS variables, the Tailwind v4 theme (theme.css), the Tailwind v3 preset, tokens.json and the base stylesheet with the component classes.
items.docs: Mockio is dark by default. With shadcn's cssVars, light is :root and dark is .dark, so add class="dark" to <html> for Mockio's default look. Or skip the cssVars and import mockio/tokens/theme.css (Tailwind v4) or the preset in mockio/tokens/tailwind-preset.js (Tailwind v3).

items.title: Mockio contracts
items.description: The contract and preview types that every component's .contract.ts and .previews.tsx import.

items.title: Mockio guidelines

items.name: action
items.title: Action
items.description: The button. One primary per view, in the accent; everything else steps down in tone.

contract.name: Action
contract.summary: The button. One primary per view, in the accent; everything else steps down in tone.

children.description: The label. Starts with a verb and says what happens, not what the button is.

tone.description: How loud the button is. Picks the fill, the ink and the press depth.

values.solid: The one primary action of the view. Accent fill, white ink, a darker edge it sinks into on press.
values.neutral: A confident secondary next to a primary, or the primary on a surface that is already accent-heavy.
values.glass: Over video or imagery, where a solid fill would cover the picture. Translucent, blurred.
values.ghost: Tertiary actions: cancel, skip, a quiet secondary in a toolbar.

withArrow.description: Adds a trailing arrow that nudges forward on hover. Only for the main path forward; it mirrors in right-to-left documents.

type.description: The native button type. Defaults to button so an Action inside a form never submits by accident; pass submit on the form's own button.

disabled.description: Greys the button and removes it from pointer events. Prefer explaining why next to it over a silent disabled state.

className.description: Extra classes, appended. For layout (width, margin) — not for restyling the tone.

onClick.description: Native click handler. Fires on pointer click, Enter and Space.

slots.name: children
slots.description: Text, optionally preceded by a 16px lucide icon with aria-hidden.

states.name: default
states.description: Resting fill for the tone.

states.name: hover
states.description: solid brightens 10%; neutral dims to 90%; ghost and glass take the lifted surface. Only on devices that can hover.

states.name: pressed
states.description: solid, neutral and glass translate down by their edge height (4px / 3px) and lose the edge; answers in 75ms.

states.name: focus-visible
states.description: 2px accent ring with a 2px offset in the page colour.

states.name: disabled
states.description: solid becomes the neutral lifted grey with faint ink and no edge; other tones drop to 40% opacity. No pointer events.

events.name: onClick
events.firesWhen: Click, Enter or Space — never while disabled.

motion: Press: transform and shadow in 75ms with the press ease-out (cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)); release in 150ms.
Arrow: translates 2px toward where it points on hover, 200ms.
Reduced motion: the press translate is instant; colour and opacity changes still run.

accessibility.role: button (native <button>)

keyboard.effect: Moves focus to the button; the focus ring appears.
Activates on release; shows the pressed state while held.

aria.note: Required only when the label is an icon alone. A visible text label is always preferred.
The trailing arrow is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
Use aria-disabled instead of disabled when the button must stay focusable to explain why it is unavailable.

accessibility.reducedMotion: Transforms are instant under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce (the system's global rule); the colour change on press remains so the press is still acknowledged.
accessibility.contrast: solid: accent-ink on accent ≥ 5:1 in both themes. neutral: surface-base on cream-bright ≥ 15:1. ghost: cream-dim on surface ≥ 4.5:1 (cream at 0.85).
accessibility.focus: focus-ring: 2px accent ring, 2px offset in surface-base. Visible only for keyboard focus (focus-visible).
accessibility.targetSize: ≥ 40px tall at the default padding (py-2.5 + 16px line); add w-full on phones for primary actions.
accessibility.screenReader: Announced as its text label and the role button. The arrow is not announced.

voice: Start with a verb, in the imperative, tú form in Spanish: "Ensayar", "Sube tu tesis", "Ver mi acta".
Sentence case. No final period. No exclamation marks.
Say the outcome, not the mechanism: "Ver mi informe" rather than "Enviar".
Free things say so in the label when price is the obstacle: "Sube tu tesis gratis".
limits: 1–4 words; ≤ 28 characters so it stays on one line at 320px.

when: Any action the user takes on purpose: start, save, send, confirm, open a flow.
The single most important next step of a screen (tone solid, often withArrow).

whenNot.situation: Navigating to another page as plain navigation
whenNot.instead: A link (<a> / router Link) styled as a link; wrap an Action in a Link only when the destination is a step forward.

whenNot.situation: Choosing one option among several
whenNot.instead: Segmented (2–5 options) or a radio group.

whenNot.situation: A destructive action with no undo
whenNot.instead: HoldButton, so a stray tap does nothing.

whenNot.situation: Toggling a setting on and off
whenNot.instead: Checkbox.

do: One solid Action per view; demote the rest to neutral or ghost.
Put the primary on the right of a pair on desktop and first in the stack on mobile.
Explain a disabled Action in text next to it.
dont: Don't put two solid Actions side by side — the user has to read both to know which matters.
Don't restyle the tone with className colours; add a tone to the contract instead.
Don't use withArrow on secondary or destructive actions.

i18n.rtl: The trailing arrow mirrors (rtl:-scale-x-100) and its hover nudge reverses; the label aligns by the document direction.
i18n.textExpansion: The pill grows with its label and wraps only inside a w-full container; keep labels short enough to stay on one line in Portuguese and German.
i18n.formatting: None: the label is the caller's text.

behaviour: Same size at every width; on phones the primary action usually takes w-full via className.
Pairs stack vertically below 360px, primary first.

designTool.placement: Anywhere an action is taken: forms, cards, toolbars, page headers. Never more than one solid per view.

differences: Defaults type to "button" so it never submits a form by accident; the app's copy relies on the native default (submit).

changes: First documented version, extracted from the product.

items.name: backdrop
items.title: Backdrop
items.description: The decorative field behind marketing heroes: slow drifting light, grain and a scrim, all CSS, and the stand-in for footage when there is none.

contract.name: Backdrop
contract.summary: The decorative field behind marketing heroes: slow drifting light, grain and a scrim, all CSS, and the stand-in for footage when there is none.

variant.description: How much light. Picks the number of lights and how far they sit from the frame.

values.hero: The full field: the pale lift from below, the navy across the top-left and a third, fainter light on the right.
values.section: A quieter field for mid-page: the lift and the navy pushed further out of frame, no third light.

still.description: Renders the same composition with no drift. For contexts that must not move — a video's poster frame, a print, a screenshot. Reduced motion stills it without this prop.

className.description: Extra classes on the layer, appended: a z-index, or a rounded corner when the parent does not clip. Not for colour.

states.name: default
states.description: The lights drift on 34s, 46s and 58s loops (the section variant runs the first two). Nothing on top of it appears to move.
states.trigger: Initial render, still={false}, no reduced-motion preference.

states.name: still
states.description: The same composition with no drift class: each light at rest in its place, at scale 1 and full opacity.
states.trigger: still={true}, or prefers-reduced-motion: reduce at mount.

motion: Three CSS loops from the preset: drift-slow (34s, translate + scale + opacity), drift-wide (46s, translate + scale) and drift-counter (58s, translate + scale + opacity), all cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.55, 1), infinite.
Only transform and opacity animate, on blurred layers the GPU composites, so the drift never triggers layout or paint.
The periods are long on purpose: a minute is slow enough that text on top never seems to move.
Reduced motion: no animation class is applied at all (see accessibility.reducedMotion).

accessibility.role: none — a presentational layer, aria-hidden

aria.note: Always set. The field carries no information.
Not ARIA, but the same promise for the pointer: clicks and taps go through to the content above.

accessibility.reducedMotion: The component calls framer-motion's useReducedMotion() and, when the user asks for reduced motion, applies no drift class — it renders exactly as still={true}, with no app-level MotionConfig needed. The preference is read when the component mounts; a change mid-visit is caught by the package stylesheet's reduced-motion block (src/styles.css), which ends every animation after 0.01ms.
accessibility.contrast: Decorative, so it has no contrast requirement of its own; it is built so that light ink over it holds AA anywhere. At its brightest point — both pale lights at full strength under the 10% middle of the scrim, about rgb(69 69 69) before grain — cream-bright text is 9.2:1 and cream-dim 6.9:1. Dark ink never goes on it. On the light theme .backdrop-field dims the whole layer to 28%.
accessibility.focus: Never focusable.
accessibility.screenReader: Nothing. Assistive technology skips the whole layer; whatever sits on top is read normally.

voice: The field has no copy. What sits on it is a hero: a short line in the product's voice, not marketing fluff — "Sustenta antes de sustentar."
The field is atmosphere, not a picture of the product. When there is footage, show the footage (HeroVideo).
limits: Copy on top: a headline and one supporting sentence; long reading text belongs on a plain surface.
examples: Un jurado de 3 que leyó tu tesis te pregunta por voz, repregunta como el de verdad y te deja un acta de 0 a 20.

when: Behind a marketing hero when there is no footage, or underneath footage while it loads (HeroVideo does both).
A mid-page marketing section that needs light rather than a flat ground (variant section).

whenNot.situation: Any signed-in screen: the thesis workspace, a rehearsal, an acta, settings
whenNot.instead: The surface tokens (surface-deep, a Panel). Nothing decorative competes with the sentence someone is reading while nervous.

whenNot.situation: There is real footage for the hero
whenNot.instead: HeroVideo, which composes Backdrop underneath as its fallback.

whenNot.situation: Behind long reading text, a form or a pricing table
whenNot.instead: A plain surface (Section on surface-deep). The drift and the grain cost legibility exactly where it is needed.

whenNot.situation: A section on the light theme that wants a soft tint
whenNot.instead: surface-deep or accent-soft. On a light page the field dims to a hint of itself, by design.

do: Give it a positioned parent that clips: relative isolate overflow-hidden.
Give the parent a dark ground (bg-black, or on-media with bg-surface-base); the field paints light, not a ground.
Put the copy above it with relative z-10.
Pass still when the field is under something that is not moving either (a paused video, a print).
dont: Don't put dark ink on it, or drop it on a light section to make a grey wash.
Don't stack two Backdrops, or add your own grain: it already has some.
Don't use it inside the app.

related.name: Section
related.difference: Owns a marketing section's rhythm and ground; Backdrop is the light inside one.

related.name: Panel
related.difference: A surface that holds content; Backdrop holds nothing and sits behind.

i18n.rtl: Does not mirror. The lights are placed physically (navy top-left, third light right) because they are a composition, not a reading direction.
i18n.textExpansion: No text of its own. It fills its parent, so longer copy on top makes the parent taller and the field follows.
i18n.formatting: None: the component renders no text, numbers or dates.

behaviour: Fills its positioned parent (absolute inset-0) at every width and clips to it.
The lights are sized in vmax, the viewport and not the parent, so the field keeps its proportions from a 320px phone to a wide desktop; a narrow frame on a wide screen shows a crop of it.

designTool.placement: As the first child of a marketing hero or section that is relative, isolate, overflow-hidden and dark. Content goes above it with relative z-10. Never inside the app shell.

differences: The pale lights read rgb(var(--cream) / α) instead of the literal rgba(222,219,200,α) — the first palette's warm cream. They are now the current ink, #F5F5F7, a touch cooler.
The layer carries on-media, so --cream resolves to the dark ink inside it in both themes and the lights stay light on the light theme.
The navy (4 33 46), which has no token, is one named constant instead of two literals; the stale "Velorah" name is gone.
Calls useReducedMotion() itself and applies no drift under reduced motion; the app's copy relies on index.css and on HeroVideo passing still.
Adds className.

changes: First documented version, extracted from the product.
Cream literals moved to the --cream token; the navy kept as a documented constant.
Reduced motion handled in the component.

items.name: badge
items.title: Badge
items.description: A small pill with a status in words — the mode of a call, a setting in force — and, when live, a breathing dot.

contract.name: Badge
contract.summary: A small pill with a status in words — the mode of a call, a setting in force — and, when live, a breathing dot.

children.description: The status in 1–3 words, optionally led by a 12px icon with aria-hidden. The words carry the meaning; nothing else does.

tone.description: Whether the status is a standing fact or something happening right now.

values.neutral: A fact about the screen: the mode ("Práctica"), a setting in force ("Modo estrés").
values.live: Something in progress at this moment ("Conectando", the interviewer's turn). Prepends an accent dot that breathes.

role.description: Native role, spread onto the span. Pass "status" when the text changes in place and the change should be announced politely.

className.description: Extra classes, appended. For layout (margin, self-alignment) — not for recolouring the pill.

slots.name: children
slots.description: Text, optionally preceded by a 12px (h-3 w-3) lucide icon with aria-hidden.

states.name: default
states.description: The lifted surface pill with cream-dim text; the live tone adds the accent dot before the text.

motion: Live dot: opacity breathes 1 → 0.35 → 1 over 2s on an in-out curve (cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.55, 1)), for as long as the tone is live. A breath rather than a blink, so it can sit beside text someone is reading.
Reduced motion: the dot does not animate and stays at full opacity. The animation class is behind Tailwind's motion-safe: variant, so the component carries its own prefers-reduced-motion check.
Nothing else moves; switching tone swaps the dot in and out without a transition.

accessibility.role: generic (native <span>); status when the consumer passes role="status"

aria.note: The live dot is decoration and is hidden from assistive technology; the words say what is happening.
Add it when the text changes in place and the change matters, like the call's turn counter. Leave it off fixed labels such as "Práctica", or every render is announced.
A leading icon passed in children must carry aria-hidden; the text names the status.

accessibility.reducedMotion: The live dot stays still at full opacity: its animation only applies under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference (motion-safe:). No provider is needed, and a change of the setting applies at once.
accessibility.contrast: Text: cream-dim on surface-lift is ≥ 9.2:1 in both themes over any surface (tightest: the light theme on surface-deep, 9.21:1). The dot is decorative (accent on the lifted pill, 2.8–5.1:1) and is never the only signal.
accessibility.focus: Not focusable.
accessibility.screenReader: Read as its text, inline. The dot is not announced, so "live" reaches a screen reader only through the words — write a status ("Conectando"), not just a name.

voice: A noun or a short status, sentence case, no period: "Práctica", "Modo estrés", "Turno 3 de 8".
Something in progress may be a gerund: "Conectando". No ellipsis — the live dot already says it is ongoing.
Numbers as digits: "Turno 3 de 8".
limits: 1–3 words, ≤ 20 characters. A badge that wraps is a sentence that wants to be body text.

when: A short fact about the current screen that the user is not changing right now: the mode of a call, a setting in force.
A status happening at this moment, with tone live: the call connecting, the interviewer's turn.

whenNot.situation: Something the user can press or toggle
whenNot.instead: Action (ghost) or Segmented. A Badge is not focusable and has no press.

whenNot.situation: Marking an option as part of the paid plan
whenNot.instead: PremiumMark.

whenNot.situation: A message about what just happened
whenNot.instead: Notice.

whenNot.situation: A score or how far along something is
whenNot.instead: Meter or ScoreRing.

whenNot.situation: Something loading, with nothing to say yet
whenNot.instead: DotMatrix, or a sentence that names what is loading.

do: Say the state in words; let the dot only add "right now".
One live badge per view at most.
Add role="status" when the text changes in place.
dont: Don't use a Badge as a button or a filter chip.
Don't make every badge live.
Don't recolour it to mean error or success.

related.name: PremiumMark
related.difference: Marks one option as paid, with a crown; Badge states a status in words.

related.name: Eyebrow
related.difference: Places a whole block above its heading; Badge describes one item or the current screen.

i18n.rtl: The dot leads the text in reading order, so it sits on the right in Arabic and Hebrew. A leading icon follows the same order; nothing is mirrored.
i18n.textExpansion: The pill grows with its text. Portuguese and German statuses run about as long ("Modo estresse", "Stressmodus"); a label too long for its row wraps inside the pill, which is the sign to shorten it.
i18n.formatting: None inside the component: a counter such as "Turno 3 de 8" arrives already formatted by the caller.

behaviour: The same size at every width.
A row of badges is the caller's flex row; give it flex-wrap so the badges drop to a second line on a 320px phone instead of overflowing.

designTool.placement: In a page header's actions, beside a title, or at the top of a card. Several sit in a flex row with gap-2 or gap-3.

differences: Accepts className and native span attributes (role, id, data-*); the app's copy takes children and tone only.
The live dot animates only under motion-safe:; the app's copy relies on the global reduced-motion stylesheet to stop it.
The live dot is shrink-0, so it keeps its size when the label wraps.

changes: First documented version, extracted from the product.

items.name: check-item
items.title: CheckItem
items.description: One row of a checklist of what a plan or an offer includes: a check in the accent, then the words.

contract.name: CheckItem
contract.summary: One row of a checklist of what a plan or an offer includes: a check in the accent, then the words.

children.description: What is included, as a short phrase. Wrapped in one span, so inline emphasis or a link stays part of the sentence.

className.description: Extra classes, appended. For spacing or a grid span — not for the ink or the check's colour.

slots.name: children
slots.description: A phrase of text; inline elements (<strong>, a link) are fine. No block content and no second icon.

states.name: default
states.description: A 16px check in accent-text aligned to the first line, then the text in cream-dim.

motion: None. A checklist enters with the card around it (the caller's FadeRise); rows do not stagger on their own.

accessibility.role: listitem (native <li>) — the consumer supplies the <ul> or <ol>

aria.note: The check is decoration and is not announced on every row.
Say what the checks mean in text before the list — a <dt>, a heading or a paragraph such as "Qué incluye" — or name the <ul> with aria-labelledby.

accessibility.reducedMotion: Nothing moves, so nothing changes.
accessibility.contrast: Text: cream-dim ≥ 9.8:1 on every page and card surface in both themes (tightest: the light theme on surface-deep, 9.89:1). Check: accent-text ≥ 4.94:1 dark, ≥ 5.19:1 light — above the 3:1 asked of a graphic, though it carries no meaning on its own.
accessibility.focus: Not focusable. A link inside the text takes its own focus ring.
accessibility.screenReader: Announced as a list item inside "list, N items", then its text. The check is not announced, so the list's label must say what the rows have in common.

voice: A noun phrase that names what you get: "Entrevistas ilimitadas", "Historial y progreso completos".
Concrete over abstract: "Tu CV en manos del entrevistador" rather than "Personalización".
Sentence case, no final period, no exclamation mark.
Rows of one list share a grammatical shape, so they scan as one list.
limits: One line where possible: ≤ 48 characters. Two lines are the most; a row longer than that is a paragraph.
examples: La empresa a la que de verdad te postulas
Tu CV en manos del entrevistador

when: Listing what a plan or an offer includes: the pricing cards, the early-access offer.
A short list of things the reader gets, where every row is a yes.

whenNot.situation: Something the user ticks or unticks
whenNot.instead: Checkbox.

whenNot.situation: Steps to follow in order
whenNot.instead: An ordered list (<ol>) with numbers; a check says done or included, not next.

whenNot.situation: Comparing what one plan has and another lacks
whenNot.instead: A table with a column per plan, so a missing feature is stated rather than implied by a missing row.

whenNot.situation: Plain bullets with no sense of included
whenNot.instead: A <ul> with a small dot, as the journey cards use.

do: Put it inside a <ul> with a label before it, such as "Qué incluye".
Keep rows of one list to the same shape and length.
Lay rows out with flex-col gap-3 on the list.
dont: Don't render a CheckItem outside a list.
Don't use a check for something that is not included.
Don't recolour the check to rank rows.

related.name: Badge
related.difference: A single status in a pill; CheckItem is one row of a list of what is included.

i18n.rtl: The check stays at the start of the row, which is the right edge in Arabic and Hebrew. The glyph itself is not mirrored.
i18n.textExpansion: Wraps under itself with the check aligned to the first line (items-start). Portuguese "A empresa para a qual você realmente se candidata" takes two lines at 320px.
i18n.formatting: None: any number in the text ("5 sustentaciones") is written by the caller.

behaviour: The same size at every width; long rows wrap and the check stays on the first line.
Spacing between rows belongs to the list (gap-3), not to the item.

designTool.placement: Only inside a <ul> (flex flex-col gap-3), usually in a pricing or offer card, below a label that says what the checks mean.

differences: Accepts className and native <li> attributes; the app's copy takes children only.
Wraps children in a single span, so mixed inline content stays one flex item; the app's copy lays each child out as its own flex item.

changes: First documented version, extracted from the product.

items.name: disclosure-mark
items.title: DisclosureMark
items.description: The pill at the end of a <details> summary that says the card opens — a chevron that turns over when open and, on larger disclosures, the word for what clicking does.

contract.name: DisclosureMark
contract.summary: The pill at the end of a <details> summary that says the card opens — a chevron that turns over when open and, on larger disclosures, the word for what clicking does.

label.description: What opening does, a verb: "Ver", "Ver planes", "Completar". Shown while closed. Absent, the mark is the chevron alone in a 32px circle.

openLabel.description: What the pill says once its <details> is open. Only rendered when label is set; "Ocultar" where the product hides a list rather than closing a card.

className.description: Extra classes, appended. For layout (-my-1 in a tight row) or, on a summary that is already on the lifted surface, a fill that separates the pill from it (bg-surface-card).

states.name: default
states.description: Closed: the lifted pill with the chevron pointing down, and the label when there is one.

states.name: open
states.description: The chevron is turned 180° (pointing up) and the label is swapped for openLabel.
states.trigger: The ancestor <details> has the open attribute: the user opened it, or <details open>.

states.name: hover
states.description: The pill lifts to cream at 14% while the pointer is anywhere on the summary, which is what tells a disclosure from a plain card.
states.trigger: The pointer hovers the summary (hover: hover and pointer: fine).

states.name: pressed
states.description: The pill scales to 0.95 while the summary is pressed.
states.trigger: The summary is :active (pointer down, or Space held).

motion: Chevron: rotates 0 → 180° over 200ms on the out curve (var(--ease-out)) when the <details> opens, and back when it closes. It turns rather than swaps, so the change reads as the same control answering.
Pill: background-color and transform transition over 150ms on ease-press (cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)) for the hover tint and the 0.95 press.
Label: the closed and open words swap instantly (display), never cross-fade.
Reduced motion: the package's global rule drops transform from transitions, so the chevron and the press change at once; the hover tint still fades.

accessibility.role: none (the whole mark is aria-hidden); the disclosure's role belongs to the native <summary>

aria.note: Always on, and not overridable: the pill and its words repeat what the summary already exposes. The browser announces the summary as expanded or collapsed.
The <summary> must carry its own visible text that names what opens ("Ajustes del ensayo"); the mark adds nothing a screen reader hears.

accessibility.reducedMotion: The chevron flips to its new direction at once and the press does not scale (transform is dropped from transitions by styles.css). The words swap instantly in every case.
accessibility.contrast: Words and chevron: cream-bright on the lifted pill, ≥ 11.6:1 in both themes over any surface (tightest: the dark theme on surface-card). The pill against the summary is decoration; the chevron's direction and the words carry the state.
accessibility.focus: Not focusable itself. The <summary> takes focus and shows the ring (pass focus-ring on it); the mark sits inside the ring.
accessibility.targetSize: not interactive itself; the whole <summary> is the target, which the caller sizes with its padding; the 32px mark sets the floor of its height.
accessibility.screenReader: Hears nothing from the mark. "Ver"/"Cerrar" are visual: a screen-reader user hears the summary's text and its expanded or collapsed state instead.

voice: label is a verb for what opening does, sentence case, no period: "Ver", "Ver planes", "Completar", "Editar".
openLabel says how to undo it: "Cerrar" for a card, "Ocultar" for a list.
The summary's own text names the thing; the label never repeats it ("Ver", not "Ver ajustes del ensayo").
limits: label and openLabel: 1–2 words, ≤ 12 characters. The pill never wraps; a long word pushes the summary's text instead.

when: At the end of a <summary> drawn as a card or a row, so it reads as something that opens: "La conversación", "Ver el detalle completo".
With a label on the larger disclosures, where the summary is a title and a line of body: "Tu plan hasta el día D" with "Ver"/"Cerrar", the plans with "Ver planes"/"Ocultar".
Icon only on rows in a list and on summaries whose text already says "Ver…".

whenNot.situation: A button that opens a menu, a sheet or a dialog
whenNot.instead: Action (ghost or neutral) with its own words; the mark only follows a <details>.

whenNot.situation: A card that navigates somewhere
whenNot.instead: A link, with Action's arrow if it needs a sign. A chevron down promises the content opens in place.

whenNot.situation: Choosing between views
whenNot.instead: Segmented.

whenNot.situation: A status of the card
whenNot.instead: Badge, beside the summary's text.

do: Put it inside a <summary>, last, with the summary's text before it.
Give the summary list-none, focus-ring and cursor-pointer, so it looks and behaves like the product's disclosures.
Use a label only where the summary is a title and a line of body.
dont: Don't put it on a button or a link: outside <summary> it never turns and its words never swap.
Don't use it to promise content that loads on a new screen.
Don't repeat the summary's text in the label.

related.name: Action
related.difference: A control with its own role and focus; DisclosureMark is a decoration inside a native <summary>, which is the control.

related.name: Badge
related.difference: A static status pill; DisclosureMark answers its <details>'s open state.

i18n.rtl: Sits at the end of the summary's row, so on the left in Arabic and Hebrew. The chevron points down and up, so it is never mirrored.
i18n.textExpansion: The pill grows with its word and never wraps (Portuguese "Preencher", "Fechar"; German runs similar). The summary's text, being min-w-0 flex-1, wraps first.
i18n.formatting: None: the words are plain strings.

items.description: A form control with its label above and an optional hint below, at the spacing every form in the product shares.

contract.name: Field
contract.summary: A form control with its label above and an optional hint below, at the spacing every form in the product shares.

label.description: What the control asks for, in a few words. Rendered as a <label> above the control: "Email", "Contraseña", "Modo por defecto".

hint.description: One or two sentences under the control: what the value is used for or the rule it must meet. Omitted, nothing is drawn below the control.

htmlFor.description: The id of the control inside, so the label names it and a click on the label focuses it. Leave it off only when the control names itself (a radiogroup or a Segmented with its own aria-label).

hintId.description: An id for the hint paragraph. Put the same value in the control's aria-describedby so a screen reader reads the hint when the control takes focus.

children.description: The control: an <input>, <select> or <textarea> carrying the field-control class and the id named in htmlFor, or a control that names itself.

className.description: Extra classes, appended to the column. For layout, such as lg:col-span-2 for a field that spans two cells of a settings grid.

slots.name: children
slots.description: One control. Native controls take className="field-control text-sm text-cream-bright" (plus placeholder:text-cream-faint when they have a placeholder, resize-none on a textarea). A self-naming control (radiogroup, Segmented) goes in without htmlFor.

states.name: default
states.description: Label in cream, the control's well (surface-card fill, line-strong border, rounded-xl) and, if given, the hint in cream-faint, 8px apart in a column.

states.name: focus-visible
states.description: Drawn by the control's field-control class, not by Field: the border takes the accent and a soft accent halo (4px at 18%) spreads around the well. The label and hint do not change.
states.trigger: The control inside receives keyboard focus.

motion: Field itself does not move.
The control's border colour and halo ease in over 200ms on the UI ease-out (var(--ease-out), cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)) when it gains focus; this is the field-control class in styles.css.
Reduced motion: unchanged. The global reduced-motion rule in styles.css keeps colour and box-shadow transitions, and this one moves nothing: it only recolours the border and fades the halo in.

accessibility.role: generic (native <div>) holding a native <label>; the control keeps its own role

aria.note: Pass htmlFor and give the control the same id. Without it the label names nothing: clicking it does not focus the control and a screen reader reads the control unnamed.

The hint is not linked to the control on its own. Pass hintId and set aria-describedby on the control to the same value when the hint carries a rule the person needs while typing ("Al menos 8 caracteres").
A radiogroup or a Segmented placed without htmlFor must carry its own aria-label, usually the same words as the Field's label.

accessibility.reducedMotion: Nothing in Field animates. The control's 200ms focus transition is a border colour and a halo, with no movement, so the global reduced-motion rule leaves it running as it is.
accessibility.contrast: Label: cream on any surface is ≥ 12.9:1 in both themes. Hint: cream-faint is ≥ 6.3:1 on dark surfaces and ≥ 4.6:1 on light ones (tightest: light theme on surface-deep, 4.61:1). The control's line-strong border is ≥ 3.5:1 against its own fill in both themes (WCAG 1.4.11), the only thing saying "this is a field" on white.
accessibility.focus: Field is not focusable. The control inside takes focus in document order and shows the field-control focus treatment: accent border and accent halo, no separate outline.
accessibility.targetSize: The label is a click target that focuses the control. The native control is full width and at least 44px tall with field-control's py-3 and text-sm.
accessibility.screenReader: The control is announced with the label's words as its name. The hint is read with it only when wired through hintId and aria-describedby; otherwise a screen-reader user meets it only by reading on past the control.

voice: Label: a noun phrase, sentence case, no colon and no period: "Tu nombre", "Modo por defecto", "Rol al que apuntas".
Hint: full sentences with a period, saying what the value is for or the rule it must meet: "Se usa para precargar las sesiones nuevas."
An optional field says so at the start of its hint: "Opcional. Nos dice qué empleador construir después."
Tú, never usted: "Empresa que tienes en mente".
limits: Label: 1–5 words, ≤ 32 characters; it does not wrap at 320px.
Hint: ≤ 2 sentences, about 140 characters.
examples: Contraseña — Al menos 8 caracteres. Una frase funciona bien.
Modo por defecto — El modo real retiene el coaching hasta el informe, como hace una entrevista de verdad. Vale más XP.
Empresa que tienes en mente — Opcional. Nos dice qué empleador construir después.

when: Any form control that needs a visible label: sign-in, reset password, settings, the early-access form.
A setting in a settings grid whose effect needs a sentence of explanation, in the hint.
A self-naming control (a radiogroup of languages, a theme Segmented) that still wants the label and hint layout.

whenNot.situation: A message about what just happened after submitting
whenNot.instead: Notice, below the fields and above the Action.

whenNot.situation: A heading over a group of fields or a block
whenNot.instead: Eyebrow, then the Fields under it.

whenNot.situation: A checkbox or toggle whose label sits beside it
whenNot.instead: A native <label> wrapping the checkbox; Field stacks the label above.

whenNot.situation: A list of what a plan includes
whenNot.instead: CheckItem.

do: Always pass htmlFor and the matching id on a native control.
Give the control the field-control class so it matches every other field.
Put the rule a value must meet in the hint, before the person types, and wire it with hintId.
dont: Don't use the placeholder as the label: it disappears as soon as someone types.
Don't put an error in the hint; the outcome of a submit is a Notice.
Don't draw a box or border around the Field; the control's well is the field.

related.name: Notice
related.difference: Says what happened after a submit; Field labels a control and explains it before.

related.name: Eyebrow
related.difference: Names a whole group or block; Field's label names one control.

i18n.rtl: The column aligns to the start edge, so label and hint sit on the right in Arabic and Hebrew. Nothing is mirrored; the control handles its own text direction.
i18n.textExpansion: Label and hint wrap inside the column at any length; the column grows downward. Portuguese and German run about 20–30% longer ("Pelo menos 8 caracteres. Uma frase funciona bem.") and still fit two lines at 320px.
i18n.formatting: None. A label with a number in it ("Duración de la entrevista — 5 turnos") arrives already formatted by the caller.

behaviour: Full width of its container at every size; field-control's w-full min-w-0 keeps a long <select> from pushing a 320px phone wider.
In a settings grid it fills one cell; className="lg:col-span-2" lets a wide field span two from the lg breakpoint.

designTool.placement: In a form or a settings Panel, stacked in a flex column with gap-5, or in a grid with gap-6. The one solid Action comes after the last Field.

differences: Accepts native div attributes (id, data-*, aria-*) spread onto the column; the app's copy takes label, hint, children, htmlFor and className only.
Adds hintId, which puts an id on the hint so the control can reference it with aria-describedby; the app's hint has no id.

items.name: mark
items.title: Mark

contract.name: Mark
contract.summary: The isologo: Mocki the parrot as three shapes on the mustard tile, in the brand's fixed colours, legible down to 16px.

size.description: Width and height in px, written as the SVG's width and height attributes. A className with h-/w- (for example h-[1.3em] w-[1.3em]) overrides it.

label.description: The accessible name. With a non-empty label the SVG becomes role="img" with that aria-label; without one (or with an empty or whitespace-only one) it is aria-hidden. Pass it only when the mark stands alone and nothing next to it already says the name. No default: decorative is the default.

className.description: Extra classes on the <svg>, appended after shrink-0. For sizing in em, a rounded corner that matches a shadow (rounded-[0.55rem] shadow-card), or margin — never for colour.

states.name: default
states.description: Decorative: aria-hidden, no role, not announced. The tile, crest, head, eye and beak in the brand colours.
states.trigger: Initial render, label omitted or empty.

states.name: named
states.description: Looks identical. Carries role="img" and the label as aria-label, so a screen reader announces it as an image with that name.

motion: None. The mark never animates: it is the one thing on the screen that stays put.

accessibility.role: none while decorative (aria-hidden); img when label is set

aria.note: Set to true when there is no label, so a mark beside the written name is not announced twice.
Set from label when it is non-empty. The text itself is the consumer's: "Mockio" is the brand name and is not translated.
Always set, so legacy Edge and IE do not put the SVG in the tab order.
A mark used as the home link keeps label empty and names the link instead: <a aria-label="Mockio">.

accessibility.reducedMotion: Nothing to reduce: the mark has no motion.
accessibility.contrast: Brand colours, not tokens, so the figures are the same in both themes. The tile is ≥ 3:1 against every surface token (tightest: surface-card on dark, 3.0:1; 5.6:1 on the light page). The white head is 5.6:1 on the tile and the eye 14.4:1 on the head. The orange beak is 2.6:1 on the tile — it is a detail of the drawing, not what identifies it.
accessibility.focus: Never focusable. When the mark is a link, the link carries .focus-ring.
accessibility.screenReader: Silent by default. With label="Mockio" it is announced as "Mockio, image" (wording varies by reader).

voice: The label, when there is one, is the brand name and nothing else: "Mockio". Not "Logo de Mockio" — the role already says it is an image.
The name is never translated: "Mockio" in every locale, so the label is not a dictionary string.
limits: label: the brand name only, one word.

when: The product's corner of the app shell, beside or instead of the written name (the top bar at 30px).
Any place the brand must be recognisable in a square: an icon tile, a compact header.
Inside Wordmark, which composes it at the height of the name.

whenNot.situation: The brand needs to be read, not only recognised (landing nav, footer, sign-in)
whenNot.instead: Wordmark — the mark and the name as one lockup.

whenNot.situation: Showing the user's progress or a friendly face in an empty state, an error or a level-up
whenNot.instead: Mascot — the full illustrated Mocki, in one of its six stages.

whenNot.situation: A decorative background behind marketing copy
whenNot.instead: Backdrop. The mark is an identifier, not a pattern; never tile or repeat it.

do: Leave it decorative when the name is written next to it, and name the link instead.
Give the tile's corner to the shadow with a matching rounded class when you add shadow-card.
Keep it at 16px or larger: it is drawn to read at favicon size and no smaller.
dont: Don't recolour it with className, filters or currentColor: the colours are the brand.
Don't rotate, stretch, outline or mirror it, in any direction or locale.
Don't put text on top of it or crop the tile.

related.name: Wordmark
related.difference: The mark and the lowercase name together; Mark alone is the square.

related.name: Mascot
related.difference: The full illustrated character with six growth stages; Mark is the reduced, fixed logo.

i18n.rtl: Never mirrors. A logo is the same drawing in every direction; nothing in the SVG reads the document direction.
i18n.textExpansion: No text, so nothing expands.
i18n.formatting: None. The only string is label, which is the caller's and, by the brand rule, always "Mockio".

behaviour: A fixed square at size px at every width; it does not scale with the viewport unless the caller sizes it in em or with a responsive class.
shrink-0, so a flex row never squeezes it into an oval.

changes: Mustard tile (#F6B733), red-orange beak (#D9481C) and ink eye (#2E2D2A), as the product's mark has been since the amber restyle.

Added the optional label for a mark that stands alone.

items.name: mascot
items.title: Mascot
items.description: Mocki, the parrot of the interview product, in one of six illustrated growth stages — from egg to crowned.

contract.name: Mascot
contract.summary: Mocki, the parrot of the interview product, in one of six illustrated growth stages — from egg to crowned.

level.description: The growth stage to draw. It is the stage, not the XP level: the product maps XP to a stage (lib/avatar.ts tierForLevel) before it reaches this component. Untyped input outside 1–6 is rounded and clamped to the nearest stage; anything that is not a finite number becomes 1.

values.2: Hatchling, cracking out of the shell.
values.3: Young parrot. The everyday face: sign-in, errors.
values.4: Headset on: practising interviews in earnest.
values.5: On a stage with a microphone and a speech bubble.
values.6: Crowned, with a medal. The end of a long curve most accounts do not finish.

size.description: Width and height in px, as the attributes. The masters are 200px, so up to 100px stays sharp on a 2x screen.

alt.description: The text alternative when the image is not decorative. The default is Spanish, with the stage number in it; pass the whole translated sentence for any other locale. An explicit empty string is respected.

decorative.description: Renders alt="" so assistive technology skips the image; it wins over alt. For a Mocki beside a heading or a message that already carries the meaning.

className.description: Extra classes on the , appended: shrink-0 in a flex row, a negative margin to tuck it over a name. Not for recolouring.

states.name: default
states.description: The stage's illustration with a soft drop shadow, and a text alternative ("Mocki, nivel 3" or the alt passed in).

states.name: decorative
states.description: Looks identical. alt="", so screen readers skip it.

motion: None of its own. An entrance belongs to the caller (PopIn on sign-in, a spring on level-up), and that caller handles reduced motion.

accessibility.role: img (native ); presentation when decorative

aria.note: Set from alt, or "Mocki, nivel {level}" by default, or "" when decorative.
The default alt is Spanish. Any other locale must pass its own alt.

accessibility.reducedMotion: Nothing to reduce: the component does not move. Wrappers that animate it (PopIn, the level-up spring) check prefers-reduced-motion themselves.
accessibility.contrast: An illustration, not text or a control, so WCAG 1.4.3 and 1.4.11 do not apply. The transparent PNG sits on any surface; the saturated mustard body reads on both themes' cards, and the drop shadow (black at 12%) only grounds it.
accessibility.focus: Never focusable.
accessibility.screenReader: Announced as its alt ("Mocki, nivel 3", image) unless decorative. Sighted users see which form it is; the default alt gives the stage as a number, not the form's description.

voice: The alt names the character and the stage, nothing more: "Mocki, nivel 3". No adjectives, no celebration.
Mocki is a name: not translated, never with an article in Spanish ("Mocki crece contigo", not "el Mocki").
Copy around Mocki follows the product voice: no exclamation marks, even at a level-up.
Beside an XP level ("Nivel 7"), pass the form wording as alt ("Mocki, forma 4 de 6") so the stage and the level are not two different numbers both called nivel.
limits: alt: under 60 characters, one phrase, no full stop.

when: The interview product's gamified layer: progress, a level-up, the habit section of the landing.
A first-run moment in the interview space, where a face lowers the stakes (the welcome checklist).
Showing which form a level earns, where the change itself is the reward.

whenNot.situation: Any screen of Sustentación, the thesis space: its landing, upload, diagnosis, rehearsal, acta and plan
whenNot.instead: No character. The thesis space speaks as a calm person beside the student, not a mascot; use Mark or Wordmark for the brand, and plain copy in a Panel or a Notice for empty and error states.

whenNot.situation: The brand logo, in a header, a favicon or a footer
whenNot.instead: Mark (the reduced isologo) or Wordmark (the lockup with the name).

whenNot.situation: A number the user needs to read: XP, a score, a level
whenNot.instead: The number as text, or Counter; Mocki shows the stage, not the value.

whenNot.situation: Waiting while something loads or the jury deliberates
whenNot.instead: DotMatrix with a sentence that says what is happening.

do: Pass decorative when a heading or a message beside it already says what is happening.
Pass a translated alt for every locale other than Spanish.
Keep it at 100px or less where it must look sharp; it is a 200px master.
dont: Don't use Mocki in Sustentación, or as the logo.
Don't recolour, crop or flip it; it carries its own colour.
Don't pair it with exclamation marks or anglicisms ("¡Mocki evolucionó! Mira su nuevo look." is the product string to fix, not to copy).

related.name: Mark
related.difference: The reduced, fixed logo; Mascot is the full character and changes with progress.

i18n.rtl: Does not mirror. The six illustrations are drawn once and are never flipped in Arabic or Hebrew: a character is not a direction, and a flipped Mocki is a different drawing.
i18n.textExpansion: No visible text. The alt can be any length in any language without changing the layout.
i18n.formatting: The only number is the stage, an integer from 1 to 6 written as a plain digit in the default Spanish alt; there is nothing to group or localise, so no Intl. A translated alt is passed whole, numbers included.

behaviour: A fixed square at size px at every width. In a flex row give it shrink-0 so long copy beside it does not squeeze it.
At phone widths keep it at 56px or less beside text; above a heading it can stay at its full size.

designTool.placement: On a card or the page ground in the interview space: beside a checklist title, above a level-up heading, at the start of an empty state. Never in the thesis space, never in a header.

differences: Renamed Mascot, and takes the stage (1–6) instead of the XP level: the level-to-stage curve stays in the product's lib/avatar.ts, so the system knows nothing about XP.
The six PNGs ship inside the component (imported as modules) instead of loading from the app's /avatars/ folder.
The alt is a prop with a Spanish default, "Mocki, nivel {level}"; the app's is a hard-coded English "Level {level} avatar, form {n} of 6".
Adds decorative, so the ten raw copies of the PNGs in the product (most of them alt="", beside Avatar rather than through it) can use the component.
Drops the axis prop, which the app's copy accepted and ignored.

changes: The six stages recoloured from violet to mustard, the same PNGs the product ships in public/avatars/.
First version: Mocki's six stages as a self-contained component, with a localisable alt and a decorative mode.

items.name: meter
items.title: Meter
items.description: A measured amount on a known scale — a score out of ten, a percentage, the XP into a level — as a label, the number and a bar that fills to it.

contract.name: Meter
contract.summary: A measured amount on a known scale — a score out of ten, a percentage, the XP into a level — as a label, the number and a bar that fills to it.

value.description: The measured amount, on the same scale as max. Printed exactly as passed; the bar clamps to 0–100% of the scale, the number does not.

max.description: The top of the scale: 100 for a percentage, 10 for a score out of ten, the XP the next level needs. A max of 0 or less draws an empty bar.

label.description: What is measured, in a word or two ("Vocabulario"). Shown above the bar on the start side and used as the meter's accessible name.

suffix.description: Written right after the number with no space: "%" for a percentage, "/10" for a score out of ten, "" for a bare count such as XP.

className.description: Extra classes, appended to the wrapper. For layout (width, a grid span, margin) — not for recolouring the bar.

states.name: default
states.description: The label and the number on one row; under them the lifted track with the accent fill scaled to value / max.

states.name: empty
states.description: The track with no fill and the number 0 beside the label. Still a meter: zero is a measurement, not a missing one.

states.name: complete
states.description: The fill covers the whole track. A value above max prints as passed (12/10) while the bar stops at full.

motion: Fill: when value changes, the bar's scaleX eases to the new proportion over 700ms on the cinematic curve (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)) — a slow settle, so a new score lands rather than jumps. A transform, so it stays on the compositor.
First render: the bar is drawn at its value with no entrance. An entrance, if the screen wants one, is the caller's (FadeRise in the product).
Reduced motion: the package's global prefers-reduced-motion rule (styles.css) drops transform from every transition, so the bar changes to its new length at once. The number never animates.

accessibility.role: meter (on the track); the wrapper is a generic <div>

aria.note: On the track, not the wrapper: a bounded measurement, not a task in progress (that is progressbar).
value, 0 and max, unclamped: a screen reader hears the same number a sighted reader sees.
Set from label, so the meter is named by what it measures.

accessibility.reducedMotion: The fill's length changes at once: styles.css removes transform from transitions under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. Nothing else moves.
accessibility.contrast: Number: cream-bright, ≥ 14:1 on every page and card surface in both themes (tightest: 14.3:1 on the dark card, 14.1:1 on the light surface-deep). Label: cream-dim, ≥ 9.2:1 in both themes on any surface. The accent fill on the lifted track is 2.8–5.1:1, a graphic that is never the only signal: the number is always printed.
accessibility.focus: Not focusable.
accessibility.screenReader: The visible label and number are read as text, then the meter is announced with its name and value ("Vocabulario, 7"). The suffix is not part of the value, so "/10" is heard only in the printed text.

voice: The label names the dimension, a noun in sentence case, no period: "Vocabulario", "Estructura", "General".
A label may carry its own count, formatted by the caller: "1240 XP en total" with suffix "".
Never a verdict in the label ("Mal vocabulario"): the number says how it went; the words around the meter say what to do next.
limits: Label: 1–4 words, ≤ 28 characters, so it stays on one line beside the number at 280px.
Number and suffix: ≤ 6 characters ("100%", "10/10").

when: A score on a fixed scale in a report: vocabulary and structure out of ten in the feedback detail.
How far into a level someone is: XP into the next level on the progress screen.
A proportion with a known top, printed as a number, where the bar helps comparing a few side by side.

whenNot.situation: Something loading or being evaluated, with no real total
whenNot.instead: A sentence that names what is happening ("Evaluando…").

whenNot.situation: A status in words, not a quantity
whenNot.instead: Badge.

whenNot.situation: The one headline score of a report
whenNot.instead: The number itself in display type; a Meter is for the supporting scores beside it.

whenNot.situation: A choice between options
whenNot.instead: Segmented.

do: Pass the suffix that matches the scale: "/10" with max 10, "" for XP.

items.name: segmented
items.title: Segmented
items.description: A pill of two to five options where exactly one is chosen, with a thumb that slides to the choice. A radio group to assistive technology.

contract.name: Segmented
contract.summary: A pill of two to five options where exactly one is chosen, with a thumb that slides to the choice. A radio group to assistive technology.

options.description: The choices, in reading order: two to five, each with a unique value. Every option gets an equal share of the track, so the widest label sets the width of all of them.

value.description: The chosen option's value. Controlled: the thumb sits under it and moves when it changes. A value that matches no option leaves nothing checked and hides the thumb.

onChange.description: Receives the new value when the person picks a different option — by pointer, arrows, Home or End. Store it and pass it back as value.

label.description: The group's accessible name (aria-label), usually the visible heading or field label beside it: "Tema", "Tiempo de exposición". Not rendered.

className.description: Extra classes, appended to the track. For layout (self-start, w-full, margin) — not for recolouring the track or the thumb.

slots.name: options[].label
slots.description: Each option's label: text of one to three words. An icon before the words is allowed only with aria-hidden; the words name the option.

states.name: default
states.description: The lifted-surface pill; unselected labels in cream-dim, semibold.

states.name: hover
states.description: An unselected label brightens to full cream. Only on devices that can hover.
states.trigger: Pointer over an unselected option (hover: hover).

states.name: focus-visible
states.description: The 2px accent focus-ring around the focused option, offset in the page colour.
states.trigger: Keyboard focus (Tab into the group, or an arrow key).

states.name: selected
states.description: The surface-card thumb sits under the option and its label turns cream-bright; aria-checked is true.

events.name: onChange
events.firesWhen: The person picks an option other than the current one: click or tap, an arrow key, Home or End. Never for the option already chosen, and never on render.

Labels: colour crossfades in 200ms on the same curve as the thumb arrives.
Reduced motion: the slide is behind motion-safe:, so the thumb appears under the new option at once; the label colour change still runs, so the choice is still acknowledged.
First paint: the thumb is already in place (it is positioned in CSS, not after a measurement), so there is no jump on load.

accessibility.role: radiogroup, with one radio (native <button role="radio">) per option

keyboard.effect: Moves focus into the group, onto the chosen option (the only one in the tab order), and out again on the next Tab.
Moves focus to the next option and chooses it; wraps from the last to the first. In right-to-left documents ArrowRight goes to the previous option instead.
Moves focus to the previous option and chooses it; wraps from the first to the last. In right-to-left documents ArrowLeft goes to the next option instead.
Moves focus to the first / last option and chooses it.
On the focused option, which is already chosen: nothing changes.

aria.note: Set from the required label prop, so the group is always named.
true on the chosen option, false on the others.
0 on the chosen option (or the first, when nothing matches value), -1 on the rest.
The sliding thumb is decoration; aria-checked carries the state.

accessibility.reducedMotion: The thumb's slide only runs under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference (motion-safe:); otherwise it moves instantly. No provider is needed and a change of the setting applies at once.
accessibility.contrast: Labels: cream-dim (cream at 0.85) on surface-lift and cream-bright on surface-card both clear 4.5:1 in both themes. The thumb is not the only signal of the choice: the label also turns cream-bright, and aria-checked states it.
accessibility.focus: focus-ring on the focused option: 2px accent ring, 2px offset in surface-base, keyboard focus only. One tab stop for the whole group; arrows move within it.
accessibility.targetSize: Each option is the track's full 44px height (min-h-11) and at least 48px wide (min-w-12); the 4px inset is drawn by the thumb, not taken from the target.
accessibility.screenReader: Announced as a radio group with the label, then each option as "radio button, checked / not checked, n of m". The thumb is not announced.

voice: Option labels are nouns or short values, not actions: "Oscuro", "Con informe", "20 min". A verb in a label means it wanted to be an Action.
Sentence case, no final period, no exclamation marks.
Parallel wording across the options, so they read as one set: "Hoja de defensa" / "Tarjetas".
Numbers as digits, formatted by the caller: "15 min".
limits: 2–5 options.
Each label 1–3 words, ≤ 20 characters; every slot is as wide as the longest, so one long label widens them all.
The group label: the field's name in 1–4 words ("Tema", "Tiempo de exposición").

when: Choosing one of two to five mutually exclusive options whose effect is immediate: the theme, a filter on a list, the length of the exposition.
Switching between two or three views of the same content in place, such as the study sheet and the cards.

whenNot.situation: Six or more options, or options that need a sentence each
whenNot.instead: A radio list (stacked radios with descriptions) or a select.

whenNot.situation: Moving between sections of a page that each have their own panel and heading
whenNot.instead: A tablist (role="tab" + tabpanel), as the settings screen does.

whenNot.situation: Running an action — copy, download, send
whenNot.instead: Action, one per action.

whenNot.situation: A single setting that is on or off
whenNot.instead: A checkbox.

whenNot.situation: Showing a status the person is not changing
whenNot.instead: Badge.

do: Keep the labels short and parallel so the slots stay narrow.
Pass a label that matches the visible field name next to it.
Apply the choice at once; a Segmented never needs a Save.
dont: Don't put actions in it: each option is a value, not a command.
Don't use it for more than five options or for long labels — it gets wider than a phone.
Don't recolour the thumb to mark one option as right or recommended.

related.name: Action
related.difference: Does something when pressed; Segmented holds which of a few values is chosen.

related.name: Badge
related.difference: States a status the person is not changing; Segmented is the control that changes it.

ArrowUp / ArrowDown, Home and End are not mirrored. Digits in labels are not mirrored.
i18n.textExpansion: Slots are equal and grow with the longest label; a label that does not fit the container wraps inside its slot (balanced, centred) and every slot grows taller together. i18n.formatting: None inside the component: labels such as "15 min" arrive formatted by the caller.

behaviour: Inline: as wide as its options need, never wider than its container (max-w-full).
Pass w-full through className to make it fill a phone's column; the slots stay equal.
On a 320px phone up to three short options sit on one line; four or five wrap their labels inside the slots.

designTool.placement: Under or beside the field label it answers, in a settings panel, a form or a list's header. Usually self-start inside a flex column so it does not stretch.

items.name: shimmer-text
items.title: ShimmerText
items.description: A word with a slow, soft light crossing it every few seconds — the one quiet flourish that says the paid plan is on.

contract.name: ShimmerText
contract.summary: A word with a slow, soft light crossing it every few seconds — the one quiet flourish that says the paid plan is on.

children.description: The text the light crosses, as a plain string: one to three words, usually the plan's name.

speed.description: Seconds the light takes to cross the text once. Higher is slower. Zero, negative or non-finite values fall back to 2.4.

pause.description: Seconds the text stays still between two sweeps. 0 runs them back to back; negative or non-finite values count as 0.

disabled.description: Stops the sweep and draws the text in the base colour, in the same box, so nothing shifts when it switches.

className.description: Extra classes, appended. For type size, weight and layout (text-xs font-semibold) — not for colour, which the tokens set.

slots.name: children
slots.description: A plain string, no elements, so the light crosses one run of text and a screen reader reads it as written.

states.name: default
states.description: The text in accent-text; once every speed + pause seconds a band of cream-bright crosses it in reading order. Left to right, each cycle opens with the pause, so the first sweep comes `pause` seconds after mount.

states.name: disabled
states.description: No sweep and no gradient: plain accent-text in the same inline-block box.

motion: One cycle lasts speed + pause seconds and repeats for as long as the component is mounted: the text stays still for `pause` seconds (4 by default), then the light crosses it in `speed` seconds (2.4 by default) at a constant rate (linear). The first sweep therefore comes `pause` seconds after mount.

Only background-position animates, from one keyframe; per-instance timing comes from an inline background-size and animation-duration. It repaints the text's own box each frame and never triggers layout — keep it to one instance per view.
Right-to-left: under :dir(rtl) the animation runs in reverse, so the light travels right to left, in reading order. There each cycle opens with the sweep and the pause follows.
Reduced motion: no sweep and no gradient; the text is drawn in the base colour.

accessibility.role: generic (native <span>) holding real text

aria.note: Deliberately absent. The visible text is the DOM text, so it is read, translated, found and selected as written.

accessibility.reducedMotion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the sweep never runs and the text is plain accent-text. useReducedMotion() from framer-motion chooses the static branch when the component mounts; a prefers-reduced-motion media query in its own <style> covers a server render and a setting changed while the page is open. No MotionConfig provider is needed.
accessibility.contrast: Every pixel is a mix of accent-text (the base) and cream-bright (the light), and in both themes the mix is never lower in contrast than the base. On the product's chip (accent-soft) that is ≥ 4.65:1 dark and ≥ 4.92:1 light at every frame; on page and card surfaces ≥ 4.94:1 dark and ≥ 5.19:1 light. Not for a surface-lift row in a dark card (4.05:1) or an accent fill (1.47:1). Selected text is drawn in accent-ink on accent (≥ 5:1). Forced-colours mode drops the gradient and draws CanvasText; print, and a browser that cannot clip a background to text, draw plain accent-text, so it never renders or prints blank.
accessibility.focus: Not focusable.
accessibility.screenReader: Read as its text, exactly as written; the light is not announced, and nothing is hidden or relabelled. A sighted reader sees the sweep; a screen-reader user loses nothing by not hearing it.

voice: A name, not a message: the plan's name as the product writes it, "Premium".
Written exactly as the name is cased; no punctuation.
Never a call to action and never a claim about the plan: the light already draws the eye.
limits: 1–3 words. The crossing takes `speed` seconds whatever the length, so on a long line the light moves faster and reads as a flicker.

when: Saying, once and quietly, that the paid plan is on for this person: the "Premium" chip in the app's top bar.

whenNot.situation: A call to action
whenNot.instead: Action with tone solid. Emphasis comes from tone, not from motion.

whenNot.situation: Marking an option as part of the paid plan
whenNot.instead: PremiumMark.

whenNot.situation: Headlines, body copy or numbers
whenNot.instead: Plain text; WordsPullUp or FadeRise for an entrance that happens once.

whenNot.situation: Showing that something is loading
whenNot.instead: DotMatrix, or a sentence that names what is loading.

do: One per view, in the chrome, on accent-soft or a page or card surface.
Pass disabled where the screen already moves (a live call, a video).
Size it with className (text-xs font-semibold), never colour it.
dont: Don't put it on an Action or any accent fill.
Don't shimmer several things at once.
Don't pass elements as children.

related.name: PremiumMark
related.difference: Marks each option that needs the paid plan; ShimmerText says once that the plan is on.

items.name: wordmark
items.title: Wordmark
items.description: The brand lockup: the Mark and the lowercase name "mockio", sized together by font-size so the logo never drifts between places.

contract.name: Wordmark
contract.summary: The brand lockup: the Mark and the lowercase name "mockio", sized together by font-size so the logo never drifts between places.

mark.description: Shows the Mark before the name, at 1.3em square. Turn it off where the mark is already on screen (the app's top bar) or a character sits right above the name (sign-in).

className.description: Size and ink, appended to the lockup's own classes: a text-* size, a weight and a colour, e.g. "text-xl font-semibold text-cream-bright". The mark scales with the font-size.

states.name: default
states.description: The Mark, a 0.35em gap and "mockio" in the mark face, lowercase, tracked -0.03em. Inherits colour and size from className or the parent.

motion: None. The wordmark is static; an entrance, if any, belongs to the container (FadeRise, PopIn).

accessibility.role: none (a plain <span>; the text is its content)

aria.note: The composed Mark has no label, so it is hidden; the visible name is what gets read.
Always set, so browser translation leaves the brand name alone.
Always set: the lockup keeps the mark before the name in right-to-left documents.
When the wordmark is the home link, the link may carry aria-label="mockio"; the visible text already gives it the same name.

accessibility.reducedMotion: Nothing to reduce: the wordmark has no motion.
accessibility.contrast: The name takes the caller's ink. With text-cream-bright, the product's choice everywhere, it is ≥ 16:1 on every surface in both themes. The mark keeps its brand colours (see Mark).
accessibility.focus: Never focusable. As a home link, the link carries .focus-ring and a rounded corner.
accessibility.screenReader: Read as the word "mockio". The mark is not announced.

voice: The component writes the name itself: "mockio", lowercase, in every locale. There is no prop to change it.
In running text the brand is written "Mockio" with a capital, as a word in the sentence — not with this component.
In Portuguese the brand takes the article in running text ("O Mockio é uma ferramenta de prática"); the wordmark itself never does.
limits: One word, fixed. Nothing is ever appended to the lockup (no tagline, no product name after it).

when: Where the brand is read, not only recognised: the landing nav, the site footer, the sign-in and unsubscribe pages.
Beside the Mark in the app's top bar on wide screens, with mark={false}.

whenNot.situation: A square place or a tight space where the name will not fit (phone top bar, icon tile)
whenNot.instead: Mark alone, inside a link named "Mockio".

whenNot.situation: The brand inside a sentence
whenNot.instead: Plain text "Mockio", capitalised, in the sentence's own font.

whenNot.situation: A friendly presence above the name on an entry screen
whenNot.instead: Mascot above a Wordmark with mark={false}; never the character and the mark together.

do: Size it with a text-* class and let the mark follow.
Use mark={false} when a Mark or a Mascot is already next to it.
Name the home link once (aria-label on the link) and keep the lockup inside it.
dont: Don't build the lockup by hand with a Mark and a text node: the size relation and the lowercase drift.
Don't capitalise it, translate it or route it through a translation function.
Don't add a tagline or a second word inside the lockup.

related.name: Mark
related.difference: The square alone, for icons and tight spaces; Wordmark adds the name.

related.name: Mascot
related.difference: The illustrated character. On sign-in it sits above a Wordmark with mark={false}.

i18n.rtl: Does not mirror. dir="ltr" on the lockup keeps the mark before the name in Arabic and Hebrew; the lockup as a whole is still placed by the page's direction (it sits at the start of an RTL nav).
i18n.textExpansion: Nothing expands: the name is the literal "mockio" in every locale, so the lockup is the same width everywhere. Neighbouring labels expand around it.
i18n.formatting: None. The only string is the brand name "mockio", which is deliberately not a prop and not translated; that is why strings is empty although the component renders text.

behaviour: Scales with font-size only; responsive sizing is the caller's (text-lg lg:text-xl).
Never wraps: one word and a square, kept on one line by inline-flex. Hide it below a breakpoint and keep the Mark instead when the row is too narrow.

designTool.placement: Start of a nav bar, a footer row or above a sign-in card. Usually inside a link home. Give it clear space of at least the mark's width.

differences: Sets dir="ltr" on the lockup, so the mark stays before the name in right-to-left locales; the app's copy flips the mark to the right of the name in Arabic and Hebrew.
Exports WordmarkProps as an interface; the app's props are an inline type.

changes: First documented version, extracted from the product.
The lockup no longer mirrors in right-to-left documents.
